Md. Sunny vs The State Of Bihar on 18 December, 2023
 In The High Court Of Judicature At Patna
 Criminal Appeal (Db) No.968 of 2023
 Arising Out of Ps. Case No.-179 Year-2021 Thana- Habibpur District-

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Patna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
======================================================
 Md. Sunny, Son of Md. Hasim Resident of Mohalla-Mahobalichak, Police
 Station-Habibpur, District-Bhagalpur.
 ... .
 Versus
 The State of Bihar

Respondent/s
 ======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Appellant : Mr. Praveen Kumar, Advocate
 For the State : Mr. Shashi Bala Verma, App
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Vipul M. Pancholi
 and
 Honourable Mr. Justice Rudra Prakash Mishra
 Oral Order

(Per: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE VIPUL M. PANCHOLI)
4 18-12-2023 Heard Mr. Praveen Kumar, learned counsel for the appellant and Mr. Shashi Bala Verma, learned counsel for the respondent-State.

2. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant has submitted that the appellant has preferred the present appeal under Section 374(2) read with Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 against the judgment of conviction dated 06-07-2023, and order of sentence dated 11-07-2023,
rendered by the learned 6th Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bhagalpur -cum- Exclusive Special Judge, POCSO Act, Bhagalpur in connection with POCSO Case No. 113 of 2021, arising out of Habibpur P.S. Case No. 179 of 2021, whereby the Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.968 of 2023(4) dt.18-12-2023 appellant has been convicted for offence punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act, and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 20 years and a fine of Rs. 1,00,000/- (One Lakh) and in default of payment of fine to suffer simple imprisonment for six months.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appeal filed by the appellant has been admitted by this Court.
However, at present the appellant prays for grant of bail and for suspension of sentence.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant referred to the deposition of the victim, and the deposition of the Doctor.

Thereafter submitted that as per the deposition given by the Doctor, age of the victim Md. Sunny vs The State Of Bihar on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164339327/
1 was between 17-19 years, at the time of occurrence, and during cross-examination, the Doctor has also stated that the age of the victim was between 17-19 years, which means; it can be 17 years, 18 years, or 19 years.
5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted from the materials placed before the Trial Court that, it can be said that the victim has voluntarily gone with the appellant, and even thereafter, as per the evidence produced before the Trial Court, Nikah also took place with the victim.
Nikahnama has also produced before the Trial Court.
Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.968 of 2023(4) dt.18-12-2023 6.

It is pointed out by learned counsel that the FIR was lodged under various Sections of IPC,
POCSO Act and under Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

Thus, it is the case of the prosecution that the victim girl got married with the present appellant, despite which the Trial Court recorded the conviction under Section 376 of IPC, as well as Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
It is also submitted that appellant was on bail during pendency of the trial for a period of more than one and half years, and he had not misused the liberty granted to him by the Trial Court.

7. On the other hand, learned APP for the respondent- State has opposed this prayer for grant of bail by contending that once the victim herself has given the deposition before the Court, and levelled the allegation against appellant, on the basis of which the Trial Court has recorded the order of conviction against the appellant, Trial Court has not committed any error.
Therefore, once the appellant is sentenced to suffer imprisonment for twenty years, this Court may not release him on bail.

8. Having heard learned counsels appearing for the parties, and having gone through the materials placed on record, prima facie, it would emerge that even as per the case of the Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.968 of 2023(4) dt.18-12-2023 victim, at the time of registration of Fardbeyan, her age was 18 years.

Even from the medical evidence, that is the deposition given by the Doctor, her age can be between 17-19 years, and the Doctor has specifically stated that 17-19 years means; it can be 17 years, 18 years or 19 years.

It is pertinent to note the prosecution has also not placed on record, the Birth Certificate or the School Leaving Certificate of the victim, and thereby, the prosecution has failed to proof with regard to the age of the victim.

It is also pertinent to note that even as per the case of the victim herself, she had gone with the appellant voluntarily at various places, and from the record, it is further revealed that Nikahnama is also placed on record.
It is not in dispute that initially the FIR, was lodged under various Sections of IPC, POCSO Act and under Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
Thus, from the aforesaid aspects, prima facie, it can be said that marriage of the appellant was solemnized with the victim- informant.
9. The aforesaid observations are prima facie observations made by this Court, and this Court does not appreciate the evidence in detail at this stage.
It is also relevant to note that appellant has remained in jail for a period of one year during pendency of the trial, and thereafter, he was released Patna High Court CR.
APP ( DB) No.968 of 2023(4) dt.18-12-2023 on bail
and during pendency of the trial, he had not misused the liberty granted to him by the concern trial court.

After the order of Md. Sunny vs The State Of Bihar on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164339327/
2 conviction recorded on 11-07-2023, he is in custody since last more than five months.

sentences.text: 10. Looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the present case, we are of the view that case of the appellant for grant of bail deserves consideration.

11. Accordingly, the appellant, above named, is ordered to be released on bail during pendency of the present appeal on executing bond of Rs. 15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand) and upon furnishing two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned 6th Additional District & Sessions Judge, Bhagalpur -cum- Exclusive Special Judge, POCSO Act, Bhagalpur in connection with POCSO Case No. 113 of 2021, arising out of Habibpur P.S. Case No. 179 of 2021 and the sentence imposed by the Trial Court is suspended so far as this appellant is concerned.
12. It is clarified that the aforesaid observations are the tentative observations made by this Court while considering the request of the appellant for grant of bail.
13. The appellant should co-
operate in this Court till disposal of the appeal.
Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.968 of 2023(4) dt.18-12-2023 14.
The sentence shall remain suspended in the meanwhile.
Realisation of fine shall also remain stayed during the pendency of this appeal.

(Vipul M. Pancholi, J) (Rudra Prakash Mishra, J) Raj Kishore/-
